source_caption:
🎬 Going in Style (2017)

Going in Style follows three lifelong friends, Willie, Joe, and Albert, who are struggling to make ends meet after spending decades working hard and preparing for retirement. Living in New York, the three elderly men find themselves facing financial uncertainty when the company they once worked for announces that their pensions are being eliminated. With bills piling up, medical expenses increasing, and the possibility of losing their homes becoming real, they begin searching for a way to regain control of their futures. After Joe witnesses a bank robbery, he comes up with an outrageous idea: rob the very bank connected to their financial troubles. Despite having absolutely no criminal experience, the three friends decide to plan an elaborate heist, leading to hilarious training attempts, unexpected mistakes, and increasingly ridiculous situations. As they prepare for their daring robbery, their friendship is tested by fear, uncertainty, and the possibility of spending their remaining years behind bars. Along the way, they discover that growing older doesn’t mean giving up on adventure, friendship, or the chance to change their lives. Combining clever comedy, heartfelt moments, surprising twists, and entertaining heist sequences, the film celebrates friendship, loyalty, second chances, and the determination to fight for a better future.

🎭 Genre: Comedy • Crime • Heist

⭐ IMDb: 6.6/10

⏱️ Runtime: 1h 36m • PG-13

🎥 Director: Zach Braff

source_details.synopsis: Going in Style is a 2017 American heist comedy film directed by Zach Braff and written by Theodore Melfi. A remake of the 1979 film of the same name, it stars Morgan Freeman, Michael Caine, Alan Arkin, Joey King, Matt Dillon, Christopher Lloyd, Ann-Margret, John Ortiz and Siobhan Fallon Hogan. It follows a trio of retirees (Freeman, Caine, and Arkin) who plan to rob a bank after their pensions are canceled. The film premiered at the SVA Theatre on March 30, 2017, and was released in the United States on April 7, 2017. It received mixed reviews from critics and grossed $85 million worldwide against its $25 million budget.
